entries.title: How can a fungus help a plant root?
entries.answer: Some fungi grow right against plant roots or inside parts of the roots. Their thin threads can reach more ground than the root could cover by itself. The fungus can pass useful minerals or water to the plant. The plant can share some of the food materials it makes using sunlight. This partnership is called a mycorrhiza. If you look at a whole tree from above ground, you may never notice the many tiny partnerships helping it below the surface.
facts: A plant and its fungal partners can share materials in both directions.

entries.title: How do fungi help a fallen log break down?
entries.answer: A fallen branch still has food materials locked inside its tough wood. Some fungi grow into the branch and release substances that break the wood down. They absorb some of the smaller pieces for food. In time, the wood can become soft or crumble. Some of its materials return to the soil or air in other forms. This work makes fungi important decomposers. A forest can keep using materials from old growth even as living trees add whole new branches and leaves.
facts: Not all fungi take apart wood in the same way.

entries.title: What part of a fungus is a mushroom?
entries.answer: A mushroom can be the visible part of a fungus that makes and releases spores. Much of the same fungus may be growing as fine threads in soil, leaves or wood. Those hidden threads collect food and can keep growing even when no mushroom is in sight. A mushroom pushes some of the fungus above the material where it lives. That can give its tiny spores a better chance of reaching the air and traveling to another spot.
facts: Many mushroom species have gills or pores where spores form.

entries.title: Where is most of a fungus hiding?
entries.answer: A fungus often grows as a net of tiny branching threads. The whole net is called mycelium. A branch can grow along the inside of a fallen stick or weave through spaces between pieces of soil. The threads can take in food after the fungus releases substances that break larger materials into smaller pieces. If a fungus makes a mushroom, the threads may stay in place after the mushroom dries out. Then a new mushroom can appear later.
facts: Many fungi have threads too thin to see well without a microscope.

entries.title: Why can lichens grow on bare rocks?
entries.answer: A lichen grows when a fungus lives closely with a partner that can make sugars using light. That partner can be a kind of alga or a kind of tiny living thing called a cyanobacterium. The fungus makes most of the sheltering body you see. Its partner helps supply food. Together they can grow on surfaces like rock, wood or tree bark. A lichen does not need to have plant roots reaching down into a pocket of soil.
facts: Lichens can have shapes like thin crusts, flat leaves or tiny branches.
